key_insight: Short-range chemical ordering in high-entropy fluorite oxides initially traps oxygen ions but, upon heating, reorganizes into interconnected transport pathways that enable mobility to exceed that of a random solid solution.
engineering_relevance: Controlling local chemical order could help optimize oxygen transport in minor-actinide-bearing mixed-oxide fuels for advanced fast reactors.
method: Hybrid Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics simulations of chemical ordering and ion transport
Comparison of short-range-ordered and random solid-solution models
Gibbs free-energy minimization and defect analysis of the superionic transition
evidence_signal: Across 2000–2800 K, simulations reveal a crossover from sluggish oxygen diffusion to enhanced mobility in the ordered model, linked to evolving polyhedral networks and superionic dynamics.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based findings without experimental validation or quantified transport gains; performance under irradiation remains to be established.
paper_title: Interplay between high-entropy effects and the superionic transition in fluorite oxides: A liquid-like perspective
